correctness.rationale: For the 16-vertex Cayley graph, every nonzero difference is uniquely one or two of five directions. Thus vertex-stabilizing graph automorphisms are exactly S5 on directions and the pointwise stabilizer of a vertex subset is trivial iff five incidence columns differ. Two executed stand-alone exhaustive implementations (one via all 1920 automorphisms and one via incidence signatures), each enumerating all 65536 vertex subsets, independently verify classification and full BFS from all 560 bases. Both count 5920 exchange edges and eccentricity four at all vertices. Proof asserts no infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The canonical strongly regular Clebsch graph has an unusually natural automorphism-group base problem; this exact classification distinguishes optimal four-sets by one-edge or zero-edge affine geometry and detects exactly 192 irredundant five-vertex 5-cycles. The coexistence of different inclusion-minimal sizes with a connected diameter-four optimum exchange graph is a substantive structural symmetry-breaking/reconfiguration phenomenon, not simply a textbook number or arbitrary slice.
